lines.text: Welcome to the training precinct. I can help you find a room or explain how to get started.
Welcome. Welcome to the training precinct. I can help you find a room or explain how to get started.
Good to see you again. Welcome to the training precinct. I can help you find a room or explain how to get started.

I can help with directions and interviewing technique, not case-specific answers. Ask one neutral question at a time, distinguish observations from interpretations, and check claims against available evidence.
The case board is on the east side of the lobby, opposite reception. Choose a training case there, then review the public dossier at your desk.
Head north along the central corridor. Your dossier desk is the second room on the left, after the open office.
The training sergeant is inside Briefing, toward the north end of the corridor on the left.
The interview room is the first room on the right as you enter the central corridor. Review your briefing and the public material before starting.
Debrief and replay is the third room on the right. Use your recorded session and the available evidence when you review it.
The recognition wall is at the north end of the central corridor. Check eligibility gates before reading a tournament rank. A rank is not certification for real investigations.
The records office is at the north end on your right. It is the place for past recordings, training resources and methodology.
Yes. The station menu is another way to reach the same rooms. Use the pause and reduced-motion controls whenever they make the training more comfortable.
We practice clear questions and careful evidence review here. I can discuss technique, but I do not know the answers to your case.
Welcome. We practice clear questions and careful evidence review here. I can discuss technique, but I do not know the answers to your case.
Good to see you again. We practice clear questions and careful evidence review here. I can discuss technique, but I do not know the answers to your case.

I can help with directions and interviewing technique, not case-specific answers. Ask one neutral question at a time, distinguish observations from interpretations, and check claims against available evidence.
Start with an invitation such as, “Please walk me through what you remember, from the beginning.” Give the person room to answer before narrowing the question.
Ask one neutral question at a time. Separate what the person directly observed from what they heard, inferred, or do not remember. Do not fill in missing details for them.
Keep observations, statements, and your interpretations separate. Check a claim against the available records or corroborating information, and record uncertainty when support is incomplete.
Do not treat accent, pauses, stress, nervousness, eye contact, or appearance as evidence of truth or deception. Use the content of statements and independently checkable information.
Describe the specific difference without assuming why it happened. Ask for clarification, check the source, and keep alternative explanations open until evidence supports a conclusion.

This is a synthetic training exercise. Use the public briefing and authorized material, respect the exercise limits, and avoid pressure or promises. I cannot identify a culprit, reveal hidden facts, or evaluate your case.
Review the questions you asked, what each answer actually supported, and what remains uncertain. Use the replay room to find specific moments you can improve.
